purpose: Explicit second-adapter selection inputs. These scores are editorial heuristics grounded in current official product-surface observations plus current support posture; they do not replace live support bundles.

criteria.description: How directly the official web/product surface exposes a logged-in browser-first entry point.
How likely the surface is to reuse the Claude shared workflow contract with minimal new abstractions.
How feasible the first baseline and route/composer bundle should be on the official browser surface.
How much the first adapter slice should teach the remaining surfaces.
How useful early support on this surface would be for GlassTTY operators.
How much fast-moving product/UI drift is likely to complicate the first proof window. Higher is riskier.

notes: General browser-native chat surface closest to the current Claude reference lane.
High lesson transfer for route detection, composer handling, submit/readback, and support-bundle shape.

Direct official browser surface with clear sign-in and prompt-entry posture.
Important for Gemini-family coverage, but developer/workspace framing may require more surface-specific abstractions earlier than ChatGPT.
Good phase-2 target once the second adapter proves the generic chat lane.
Official web surface exists and is operator-relevant, but route churn and product velocity raise first-proof risk.
Search/X-integrated posture may complicate latest-turn semantics compared with the Claude/ChatGPT lane.
Very rich browser work surface with docs/slides/sheets/websites affordances.
Potentially high operator value, but the richer workspace surface likely widens complexity sooner than the second adapter should.
Clear chat/API browser surface with a plausible general chat lane.
Likely useful, but not as obviously transferable as ChatGPT and not as strategically urgent as AI Studio in the current staged rollout.
